neighbours.label: the point where an attempt turns out to lead back to the starting problem: 'back to square one', 'going in a circle', 're-created the same ...', 'only half the problem' (the output promotes ' still' / ' again'); the same effort told as a success stays quiet
fire: We replaced the pump last spring, and by autumn we were back to square one.
Each new diet works for a month, and then she is right back where she started.
The committee argued for hours and ended up going in a circle.
They rewrote the software from scratch but only re-created the same old bugs.
If the city just widens the road, it only solves half the problem.
He paid off one credit card with another and found himself back at the beginning.
After three reorganisations the department had simply rebuilt the same silos.
The peace talks collapsed, and both sides were once again at square one.
quiet: We replaced the pump last spring, and by autumn the garden was thriving.
Each new recipe takes a month to learn, and then she teaches it to her friends.
The committee argued for hours and ended up approving the budget.
They rewrote the software from scratch and shipped it two weeks early.
If the city widens the road, the buses will run on time.
He paid off one credit card after another and bought a small house.
After three reorganisations the department had doubled its output.
The peace talks succeeded, and both sides signed the treaty on Friday.

notes: Card: no single token (' that', ' back', ' to', ' only', ' no'); examples: 'back to square one', 'going in a circle; the underlying assumption', 're-created the same programs', 'only take care of half the problem'; direct effect promotes still / again / unresolved. Probes: back to square one 0.80, only half the problem 0.49, re-created the same broken process 0.41; the roof stays dry 0.05; 'the issue remains unresolved' only 0.06, so it is the circling-back turn, not unresolvedness as such.
